{{Short description|Sequence of field extensions in mathematics}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2026}}

In [[mathematics]], specifically [[number theory]], a '''tower of fields''' is a sequence of [[field extension]]s
:<math>F_0 \subseteq F_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq F_n \subseteq \cdots</math>
A tower of fields may be finite or [[infinite sequence|infinite]].

==Examples==
* <math>\Q \subseteq \R \subseteq \C</math> is a finite tower of the [[rational number|rational]], [[real number|real]] and [[complex number]]s.
* The sequence obtained by setting <math>F_0 = \Q</math> and letting
::<math>F_n = F_{n-1}\big(2^{1/2^n}\big)</math>
:for <math>n\geq 1</math> (i.e. <math>F_n</math> is obtained from <math>F_{n-1}</math> by [[adjunction (field theory)|adjoining]] a <math>2^n</math>-th [[nth root|root]] of <math>2</math>) is an infinite tower.
* Similarly, if <math>p</math> is a [[prime number]], the '''''p''th [[cyclotomic]] tower''' of <math>\Q</math> is obtained by setting <math>F_0 = \Q</math> and letting <math>F_n</math> be the field obtained by adjoining to <math>\Q</math> the <math>p^n</math>-th [[root of unity|roots of unity]]. This tower is of fundamental importance in [[Iwasawa theory]].
* The [[Golod–Shafarevich theorem]] shows that there are infinite towers obtained by iterating the [[Hilbert class field]] construction to a [[number field]].
